quiz.title: Chapter 11 Quiz: Advanced Administrative Research
quiz.intro: Ten questions on guidance, adjudication, deference after Loper Bright, and recording an authority level for everything you find.

items.q: A question about what a vague regulatory term (“adequate ventilation”) requires in operation points to:
options: The Federal Register preamble only
Interpretive guidance, compliance manuals, and opinion letters
Administrative adjudication decisions
Enforcement statistics
items.why: A question about how the agency applied the rule to facts points to adjudication; a question about priorities points to enforcement guidelines (Advanced Administrative Materials and the Research Cycle).

items.q: This chapter asks you to add one thing to every Research Log finding. What is it?
options: A docket number
The authority level, stated at the start of the Findings field: binding regulation, persuasive guidance, or advisory
The agency’s phone number
A Westlaw headnote
items.why: Skipping it is how a persuasive gloss migrates into your outline dressed as the rule (Advanced Administrative Materials and the Research Cycle).

items.q: Skidmore v. Swift & Co. stands for:
options: Courts must defer to agency guidance
Courts may give guidance persuasive weight in proportion to the agency’s expertise and the thoroughness of its reasoning
Guidance documents have the force of law
Agencies cannot issue guidance
items.why: Guidance is influential but not binding (Guidance Documents: Influential but Not Binding).

items.q: After Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024):
options: Courts defer to an agency’s reasonable reading of an ambiguous statute
Courts independently determine the best interpretation of ambiguous statutes rather than accepting the agency’s view
Agencies can no longer issue regulations
Skidmore was overruled
items.why: Chevron was overruled; Skidmore weight for informal guidance remains (Post-Loper Bright).

items.q: Administrative adjudication decisions are valuable because they:
options: Have the force of a statute
Apply the regulation to specific fact patterns, the application analysis a bare regulation cannot give you
Are always published in the CFR
Bind every federal court
items.why: They may function as precedent within the agency, subject to judicial review (Administrative Adjudication).

items.q: Which is the best place to find a federal agency’s guidance documents?
options: The Statutes at Large
The agency’s own website or electronic reading room, with Regulations.gov and the Federal Register as supplements
Google Scholar
PACER
items.why: Commercial databases carry selected guidance, but coverage is not comprehensive (Searching for Advanced Administrative Materials).

items.q: FOIA is a poor tool when:
options: The agency is federal
The clock is running, since responses can take months or years
You want internal documents
You are doing scholarly research
items.why: FOIA is valuable for thorough compliance or scholarly research, not urgent matters (FOIA as a Research Tool).

items.q: Representing a guidance document as binding law is:
options: Standard practice
A professional error, and after Loper Bright an increasingly consequential one
Acceptable if the agency enforces it
Required by Rule 3.3
items.why: “Legally required” versus “the agency’s preference” is the line a client pays you to draw (Evaluating Administrative Authority).

items.q: Your question is “has the FTC taken enforcement action against this type of marketing claim?” That is:
options: A definitional question answered by the CFR
An application question answered by enforcement actions and adjudication, past the CFR text
A survey question for an ALR
A question for legislative history
items.why: These questions push past the regulation to the full range of materials agencies produce (Questions This Source Answers).

items.q: The chapter links Chapter 10 and this one with what common question?
options: Which database is cheapest
How much weight a court should give an account of a statute’s meaning that the court did not write and the enacted text does not contain
Whether agencies are part of Congress
Whether the CFR is binding
items.why: After Loper Bright, an agency’s reading, like legislative history, is something a court may find persuasive, not something it must accept (Post-Loper Bright).

drills.title: Authority Level
drills.blurb: Eight agency documents. State the authority level you would open each Findings entry with.
